evidence.quote: This paper presents an organization-adaptive framework combining a structured survey, causal inference, and clustering to uncover actionable drivers of developer satisfaction.

The final instrument comprised 74 five-point Likert-scale items spanning these six categories. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was applied to the collected responses to assess construct validity prior to causal modeling.
Second, we estimate the directed relationships among these factors using the direct linear non-Gaussian acyclic model (DirectLiNGAM).
The number of clusters was determined using the elbow method on within-cluster sum of squared errors across k = 2–9, yielding five clusters.
As a case study, we applied the framework to Panasonic Automotive Systems Co., Ltd. (PAS), a large Japanese automotive software organization. The survey targeted 42 developers
Across all categories, productivity exerted the strongest direct effect on satisfaction, whereas creativity exerted a strong indirect effect through productivity.
The first stage measures developer satisfaction through a survey organized around six categories: Product, Process, Environment, Team, Individual, and Project.
